chunks: And Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him and said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what is the blood-money (diyah) of the child of zina?' He said, 'The one who spent on him is given what he spent on him.' I said, 'If he died and he had wealth, who inherits him?' He said, 'The Imam.'

key_terms.أَنْفَقَ عَلَيْهِ: He spent on him (referring to the father's provision)
key_terms.الإِمَامُ: The Imam (specifically in the context of inheriting the child of zina)
key_terms.دِيَةُ: Blood-money or compensation paid for death or injury

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the wealth of a child of zina according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific financial status of *ibn al-zina* (child of fornication), distinguishing between the right to reimbursement of maintenance expenses (*diyah* in this context) and inheritance rights. It establishes that while the father who provided for the child is entitled to recover his expenditures upon the child's death, the child's remaining wealth reverts to the Imam, reflecting the Shia view that the child has no direct lineage-based inheritance from the father unless explicitly acknowledged or provided for.
